evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/voice_webhooks.rs:198-307 (alexa_webhook) takes `mut rls: RlsConnection` as an extractor (checks out a pool connection + sets tenant/RLS context). Its SUCCESS and account-link paths correctly call `rls.release().await` (lines 233 and 305), but EVERY error path returns without releasing: signature-verification failure returns Err at 205-210, body-parse failure at 214-223, `authenticate_voice_user(rls.conn(), ...).await?` at line 230, and the two `process_command(...).await.map_err(...)?` sites at 257-263 and 279-285. The `?` operator and the early `return Err(...)` statements all return before any release() call runs.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/voice_webhooks.rs:337-404 (google_actions_webhook) is inconsistent with itself: it DOES release on the Google-ID-token verify-failure path (line 347) and on the success/link paths (367, 402), but still skips release on the `?`-propagated error paths — `authenticate_voice_user(...).await?` at line 364 and `process_command(...).await.map_err(...)?` at 391-400. So even the more-careful of the two handlers leaks release() on auth/processing errors.

backend/crates/api-core/src/extractors/rls_connection.rs:197-221 — `impl Drop for RlsConnection` is a safety net: when dropped without release() it emits `tracing::warn!(... "RlsConnection dropped without calling release() - spawning cleanup task. Call rls.release().await before handler returns for guaranteed cleanup.")` and calls `db::tenant_context::spawn_clear_context(...)`. The explicit `release()` (lines 143-168) instead AWAITS `clear_request_context` before the connection returns to the pool. Because Drop clears the context (via a spawned task), this is NOT a cross-tenant RLS leak — the impact is operational, not a security hole.

Impact: the voice webhook endpoints (POST /api/v1/webhooks/voice/alexa and /google) are UNAUTHENTICATED public receivers — anyone can POST. Every forged/invalid request (fails at signature/ID-token verification) and every downstream processing error therefore produces a warn-level 'RlsConnection dropped without calling release()' log line plus a spawned cleanup task, instead of a clean awaited release. Under a burst of forged requests this is a cheap log-amplification / task-spawn vector that also masks the warning's intended diagnostic value. It also violates the contract documented in routes/integrations/webhook.rs ("Every authenticated path calls rls.release().await before returning") and the Drop warning's own instruction.

Confidence MEDIUM (static-only): both handler bodies and the RlsConnection Drop/release impls were read directly and the missing release() on the error branches is unambiguous; not runtime-confirmed (no compilation/test execution on this cloud runner). Severity LOW (+1): the Drop safety net guarantees context is cleared and the connection returns to the pool, so there is no data leak or connection exhaustion — the defect is a documented-contract violation plus warn-log/task amplification on a public endpoint.

Fix direction: capture the Result of the fallible steps, call `rls.release().await`, then return/propagate — e.g. replace `let device = authenticate_voice_user(rls.conn(), token, ...).await?;` with a match that releases on the Err arm before returning, and do the same for the `process_command` sites and (for Alexa) the signature/parse-fail early returns. This mirrors the verify-fail path in google_actions_webhook (line 347) that already releases correctly. Alternatively restructure each handler so a single release() runs on all exits (inner async fn returning Result, release after it).
